page.overview:
What is Goldfinger?

Goldfinger is a 1964 spy film, and the third film in the James Bond series as well as the third to star Sean Connery as the MI6 agent James Bond. The main cast was rounded out by Gert Fröbe and Honor Blackman. The film was produced by Albert R. Broccoli and Harry Saltzman, and was the first of four Bond films directed by Guy Hamilton.

The film is generally regarded as the first official Bond blockbuster as well as being the template for all future Bond films; it is usually credited with triggering what is known as the "James Bond craze". The film made cinematic history when it recaptured its production costs in record-setting time, despite a budget equal to that of the two preceding films combined. Goldfinger was also the second Bond film to use a pop star to sing the theme song during the titles, the first being "From Russia With Love, sung by British pop star Matt Monro. Every other Bond film would include a pop star song, except On Her Majesty's Secret Service. This is also the last Bond film to use the original Bob Simmons Gunbarrel sequence, which was first used in Dr. No.

After foiling a heroin operation in Mexico, James Bond travels to Miami to relax. While there, he is approached by Felix Leiter, who makes Bond aware of the presence of wealthy metallurgy entrepreneur Auric Goldfinger. After Bond spoils Goldfinger's gambling fraud with help of latter's female aide-de-camp, Goldfinger retaliates by having the woman killed. Upon return to England, M assigns Bond investigate Goldfinger, who is suspected of gold smuggling. Shadowing Goldfinger, Bond comes to learn of former's scheme targeting United States' gold reserve in Fort Knox in Kentucky.

The movie starts in Mexico, where James Bond stealthily swims to a pier of a Mexican port. Bond gets out of the water and - by using a grappling gun - gets over a wall into the drug manufacturing complex. After taking out a guard, Bond finds a entrance to one of the drug labs and sets plastic explosives with a timer and leaves.

Also known as: Goldfinger film, Goldfinger (film).
